full_judgment: 3. The defendant opposite party contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaint and contending inter alia that the land measuring 8 acres appertaining to CS Khatian No.1272 of Mouza No.3 Baniakhamar originally belonged to Mukta Boishnabi who was survived by two sons namely Santosh Kumar Howlader and Sudhir Kumar Howlader. On 10-6-1943 Santosh transferred 2½ acres to Gnndra Nath Dey and Nitai Chand Dey by way of Kabala. Sudhir transferred 11/4 acre to said Girindra and Nitai. Grindra and Nitai leased out the land together with a tin made house on it to Lotan Sohani and Jamini Sohani. Thereafter, the defendant opposite party, with prior permission of Grindra and Nitai, took possession of the land from Lotan and Jamini for a consideration of Taka 6,000. From that time he has been possessing the land. On 28-1-1967 Girindra and Nitai executed a Bainanama in favour of the defendant opposite party to sell the property to him at Taka 5,000 and accordingly took Taka 4,600 on several occasions. Subsequently Girindra and Nitai left Bangladesh for India without executing any Kabala favouring the defendant opposite party. Since then he has been holding the property for more than 12 years in adverse possession and hence in the disputed land the plaintiff has no title at all.
